primary-500.note: The only accent: primary action or on-state. Ramp pinned at 500 #ff5a3c and 700 #c8331a, derived in OKLCH at their hue.

accent-surface.note: Fill of filled accent controls, paired with accent-on. Light #c8331a with #ffffff (5.3:1); dark #ff5a3c with #1d0a05 (6.2:1). White on #ff5a3c is 3.1:1 and fails.

surface-card.note: Raised reading surface and menus (also surface-dropdown). #ffffff / #181a21.

surface-chrome.note: surface-header, surface-footer, surface-sidebar: the page ground, divided by a border-default rule.

surface-hover.note: Hover fill of neutral controls and rows. #d3d3cb / #2b2f3a.

text-muted.note: Secondary copy and metadata. #5c606b / #a4a8b4; at least 4.5:1 on the page ground and on a card.

surface-release-row.note: Transparent: rows are hairline-divided (border-release-row = border-default), not filled.

chips.note: --chip-<kind>-bg/-fg with -dark twins: media, nfo, preview, sample, completion-ok/-mid/-low, res-4k/-1080/-720/-sd, mi-* media-info hues. From docs/proposals/tv-redesign/prototype/reference/tokens.json. Status colours, never the accent.

display.purpose: Page titles at sm and above; weight 800. Rare.

headline.purpose: The x-page-header title, with an accent icon.

body.purpose: The 14px baseline. The app's dominant size by a wide margin.

label.purpose: Chips, badges, metadata, table headers, small controls.

modes.name: dark
modes.note: Class-based: @custom-variant dark (&:where(.dark, .dark *)). A per-user choice; each token has a -dark twin.

shadows.name: card
shadows.purpose: Gentle lift on .card, on top of its 1px border. Borders lead; shadow is secondary.

shadows.name: dropdown
shadows.purpose: Menus and popovers floating above the page.

shadows.name: modal
shadows.purpose: Dialogs, the deepest level in the stack.

shadows.name: floating
shadows.purpose: --shadow-floating: menus, dialogs, search results and the selection bar on redesigned screens, with no border.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Body background-colour transition on theme change, 200ms.

motionGaps.name: prefers-reduced-motion
motionGaps.note: Zero occurrences across resources/ as of 2026-09-20, while csp-safe.css ships transitions and fadeIn/pulse keyframes. Recorded as an observed gap, not a rule.

extensions.breakpointsNote: Tailwind v4 defaults. The project overrides none of them; there is no tailwind.config file.

outOfScope.name: forum
outOfScope.note: Separate preset, own Vite entrypoint and x-forum::button family.

outOfScope.name: pulse
outOfScope.note: Laravel Pulse uses Livewire and its own styling.

outOfScope.name: admin control sizes
outOfScope.note: Admin keeps its existing component sizes; the .public-ui scale does not apply there.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Default action: the accent pair (accent-surface with accent-on). Bordered even though filled, so the shape holds on any surface.
components.css: .ds-btn { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; justify-content:center; gap:0.5rem; height:42px; padding:0.5rem 1rem; border-radius:0.5rem; border:1px solid transparent; font-family:Manrope,ui-sans-serif,system-ui,sans-serif; font-size:0.875rem; font-weight:600; line-height:1.5; cursor:pointer; transition:background-color 150ms cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-btn:focus-visible { outline:none; box-shadow:0 0 0 2px #fff,0 0 0 4px var(--color-primary-500,#ff5a3c); } .ds-btn-primary { background:var(--accent-surface,#c8331a); border-color:var(--accent-surface,#c8331a); color:var(--accent-on,#fff); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background:var(--color-primary-800,#9a2b19); }

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Neutral action beside a primary one.

components.name: Input Control
components.description: The shared public control scale: 42px tall, 8px radius, 14px text. Applies where the control is inside .public-ui; outside it, x-input's own utility baseline renders instead.
components.css: .ds-control { height:42px; padding:0 14px; border-radius:8px; border:1px solid var(--border-default,#d3d3cb); background:var(--surface-card,#fff); color:#374151; font-family:Manrope,ui-sans-serif,system-ui,sans-serif; font-size:14px; line-height:1.5; } .ds-control:focus { outline:none; border-color:var(--color-primary-500,#ff5a3c); box-shadow:0 0 0 1px var(--color-primary-500,#ff5a3c); }

components.name: Card
components.description: The raised reading surface. Border defines it; shadow lifts it slightly. .card owns no padding in the source — the 1.5rem here exists only so the snippet renders.
components.html:
Release

Border leads, shadow is secondary.
components.css: .ds-card { background:var(--surface-card,#fff); border:1px solid var(--border-default,#d3d3cb); border-radius:0.75rem; box-shadow:0 4px 6px -1px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1),0 2px 4px -2px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1); padding:1.5rem; font-family:Manrope,ui-sans-serif,system-ui,sans-serif; } .ds-card-title { margin:0 0 0.5rem; font-size:1.125rem; font-weight:600; color:#111827; } .ds-card-body { margin:0; font-size:0.875rem; color:var(--text-muted,#5c606b); }

components.name: Chip
components.description: A readout, not decoration. Reports completion, preview availability, origin or category.
components.css: .ds-chip { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; gap:0.25rem; background:var(--surface-panel-alt,#e4e4dd); color:#374151; border-radius:0.5rem; padding:0.125rem 0.5rem; font-family:Manrope,ui-sans-serif,system-ui,sans-serif; font-size:0.75rem; font-weight:500; line-height:1.5; } .ds-chip-success { background:#dcfce7; color:#166534; }

components.name: Badge
components.description: The pill form. Five tones, three sizes, always fully rounded.
components.css: .ds-badge { display:inline-flex; align-items:center; background:var(--color-primary-100,#fde7e2); color:var(--color-primary-800,#9a2b19); border-radius:9999px; padding:0.125rem 0.625rem; font-family:Manrope,ui-sans-serif,system-ui,sans-serif; font-size:0.75rem; font-weight:500; }

narrative.maintainerStatement: Visually appealing, easy to navigate, and easy to absorb the information being shown.
narrative.overview: NNTmux is a catalogue you retrieve from, lit well enough that you can read it. The collection is enormous and mostly machine-generated, so the interface's job is to make a wall of releases legible: what this thing is, whether it is complete, whether it is worth taking. Chips are the instrumentation and they are read at a glance rather than studied. The system serves two audiences on one chassis: the public side browses, searches and evaluates; the admin side operates the indexer that fills it. There is one accent, coral, meaning the primary action or 'this is on'; light and dark are a per-user choice. Every value is reached through tokens, so the vocabulary is replaced by editing resources/css/app.css.
keyCharacteristics: One coral accent; light and dark themes, chosen per user
Warm-neutral grounds; header, footer and admin sidebar sit on the page ground behind a hairline
A 14px body baseline on existing pages: the app reads dense even where controls are comfortable
One text family, Manrope, carrying the whole hierarchy by weight and size
Borders define surfaces; shadow is a gentle secondary lift
Status colour is semantic and literal; the accent belongs to actions, navigation and on-states

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Coral means primary action or this-is-on, on every screen. No decorative coral and no second accent. Reach it through primary-* or the accent pair; a literal value is a status colour and should say so.

rules.name: The Chip Is a Readout Rule
rules.body: Chips report state; they are not decoration and not navigation by another name. A chip that does not tell the reader something they would otherwise have to open the release to learn does not belong on the row.

dos: Use primary-* for accent text, links, focus rings and tinted selected states.
Fill accent controls with --accent-surface and --accent-on, never primary-* with white.
Give every colour utility a dark: counterpart unless a token or ancestor handles it.
Reuse x-button, the input/select/textarea/label set, and the semantic surface classes.
Put styles in csp-safe.css or utilities; the Alpine CSP build rejects inline style attributes.
Keep status colour literal and semantic.
donts: Don't reintroduce a colour-scheme choice; coral is the only accent.
Don't introduce a second text family or a second icon library.
Don't reach for shadow where a border would do, outside the floating layers of redesigned screens.

enforcement.runsIn: frontend verification lane; scripts/agent-verify gates it behind `if frontend:`, and it is a required CI command in .github/ci-policy.json
enforcement.principle: Every check inspects class names, not values. The rules constrain how a value is reached, never what the value is. A redesign that replaces palette, type scale, spacing and component language passes all of them untouched, provided it routes through the token layer. See the script's own comment at line 26: views reach the accent through tokens so app.css can replace it.

indirectionRules.rule: no literal blue-* accent utility in views; use primary-*
forum primary-* utilities need an explicit dark: treatment
no hardcoded bg-white / bg-gray-N in public views; use semantic surfaces or tokens
no indigo-*/purple-* accent utilities in public views; use primary-*
no blue-* accent utility assigned from JavaScript; use primary-*
nothing selects or stores a colour scheme (data-color-scheme, colorScheme, color_scheme, setScheme)

hygieneRules.rule: no Bootstrap btn shim; use x-button / x-button-link
Font Awesome is the only icon library (no feather)
hygieneRules.open: whether a replacement design keeps this constraint is deliberately unsettled

hygieneRules.rule: no inline style attributes; CSP constraint, not a preference
fixed Vue action panels need v-cloak

hygieneRules.open: tied to the icon-library question above

enforcement.descriptiveOnly: narrative.dos and narrative.donts below, and everything else in DESIGN.md, are description rather than law. No check inspects them and a redesign may overturn any of them.
